name: Japan

eSignLaw.name: Act on Electronic Signatures and Certification Business
eSignLaw.citation: Act No. 102 of 2000, Article 3; Civil Code Article 522(2)

levelNote: Contracts generally need no particular form, so a simple electronic signature can be enough as evidence of agreement.
ageNote: Japan lowered the age of majority from 20 to 18 in April 2022.

formRequirements.note: Wills must be handwritten, or made by notarial deed or in secret; electronic wills are not recognised.

notices: Electronic signature law that applies: Act on Electronic Signatures and Certification Business. Contracts generally need no particular form, so a simple electronic signature can be enough as evidence of agreement.
You must be at least 18 years old to sign this agreement. Japan lowered the age of majority from 20 to 18 in April 2022.
If you are unsure whether this applies to you, ask for a paper alternative before signing.
limitationNote: Five years from knowledge, ten from when the claim could first be exercised (Civil Code art. 166).
